feed.title: Tools & Utilities — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: .NET Fiddle
entry.summary: Write, run and share C# and .NET code in the browser — no install.

entry.title: Browser Diet
entry.summary: A guide of concrete, measurable tips for improving web performance.

entry.title: Browserling
entry.summary: Live-test your site across different browsers and operating systems.

entry.title: Can I email…
entry.summary: A table showing which email client supports an HTML/CSS feature. Unlike the web’s Can I use it looks at the quirky, limited support of email clients.

entry.title: Cmder
entry.summary: A portable, pleasant console package for Windows that ships with bash and unix commands. Unlike the built-in cmd it offers tabs, themes and unix tools together.

entry.title: Cmder
entry.summary: A portable, pleasant Windows console that can run bash and unix commands.

entry.title: Comcast
entry.summary: Injects network latency and packet loss to test how software copes under bad conditions.

entry.title: ConnectionStrings.com
entry.summary: A reference giving the correct connection-string format for every database and driver. Unlike hunting the docs it gathers the syntax of dozens of drivers in one place.

entry.title: Coursier
entry.summary: A fast JVM dependency resolver and application launcher written in pure Scala.

entry.title: docsify
entry.summary: A tool turning Markdown files into a documentation site in the browser, with no build. Unlike static generators it has no build step — it serves the pages on the fly.

entry.title: Editor.md
entry.summary: An open-source, in-browser Markdown editor with live preview and export.

entry.title: ES6 Console
entry.summary: A console that compiles modern JavaScript (ES6+) in the browser and shows the result instantly.

entry.title: Firefox Developer Edition
entry.summary: A build of Firefox for web developers, with advanced debugging tools built in.

entry.title: Full Page Screen Capture
entry.summary: A Chrome extension that captures an entire page — scrolling included — as one image.

entry.title: generatedata
entry.summary: A tool generating realistic fake test data to a given schema (CSV, JSON, SQL). Unlike making data up by hand it produces fields like names and addresses consistently and in bulk.

entry.title: Google Safe Browsing
entry.summary: Checks whether a site is flagged as unsafe in Google’s Safe Browsing records.

entry.title: Hyper
entry.summary: An open-source terminal built with web technologies and extensible via plugins.

entry.title: Invertexto
entry.summary: A site bundling small text utilities — reversing, counting, converting and more.

entry.title: JCTools
entry.summary: Very high-performance concurrent queues for the JVM, used by projects like Netty.

entry.title: JitPack
entry.summary: Makes GitHub repos that don’t publish jars usable directly as dependencies.

entry.title: Joomla
entry.summary: An open-source content management system (CMS), an alternative to WordPress.

entry.title: JSCompress
entry.summary: A tool that minifies JavaScript in the browser to shrink its size.

entry.title: JSON Editor Online
entry.summary: A browser tool to inspect and edit JSON in tree and text views. Unlike a plain editor it folds and validates the structure, making large JSON easy to navigate.

entry.title: JSON Sort
entry.summary: A simple tool that alphabetically sorts and formats JSON keys.

entry.title: KeyCDN Tools
entry.summary: Bundles network tools like ping, traceroute, HTTP header and performance tests.

entry.title: Liveweave
entry.summary: An in-browser playground to try HTML, CSS and JS with live preview.

entry.title: Lorem Ipsum
entry.summary: The classic generator of placeholder text (lorem ipsum) for design mockups.

entry.title: Memcached
entry.summary: A distributed memory cache that speeds up sites by holding hot data in RAM.

entry.title: Mockaroo
entry.summary: Generates realistic fake test data (CSV, JSON, SQL) to your chosen schema.

entry.title: OnlineGDB
entry.summary: An online IDE that compiles and debugs C and many languages in the browser (gdb included).

entry.title: Pants
entry.summary: A build system that scales to large, multi-language monorepos (originated at Twitter).

entry.title: Password Generator
entry.summary: A simple, security-focused password generator with adjustable length and character sets.

entry.title: RESP.app
entry.summary: A GUI for Redis — view, edit and delete data in your instance.

entry.title: Scalastyle
entry.summary: A linter that checks Scala source against formatting and style rules.

entry.title: Scoverage
entry.summary: A statement-based code-coverage tool for Scala, more precise than line-based coverage.

entry.title: Swagger
entry.summary: An OpenAPI toolset to design, document and try RESTful APIs.

entry.title: Tools of the Trade
entry.summary: A list of tools used by companies on Hacker News.

entry.title: Wappalyzer
entry.summary: Reveals which technologies (framework, server, analytics) a website runs on.

entry.title: web.dev
entry.summary: Google’s guides and measurement tools for web quality — performance, accessibility, PWA.

entry.title: Website Grader
entry.summary: A free tool that grades a site on performance, SEO, mobile and security.
